transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I guess… the main thing is that I’m having trouble making sense when I talk or write, especially around my work. I’m an artist, so I’m used to explaining ideas in a more abstract way, like textures and mood and symbolism, but lately it’s been different. My artist statements will start out about, say, the surface of a material or why I chose a certain color, and then suddenly I’m talking about a budget issue, and then somehow I’m explaining what feels like a hidden meaning behind a client’s wording, and I don’t always notice the jump until someone points it out.

It’s happening in client notes too, which is embarrassing because those are supposed to be straightforward. And in meetings I’ll be trying to explain something simple, but I’ll sort of leap from one idea to another, like textures to costs to… I don’t know, patterns or meanings I think are important, and people keep saying they can’t follow me. They’ll ask me to start over, or they’ll look confused, and then I get flustered because in my head it feels connected. That’s why I came in.
Have you felt unusually energized lately, like you need much less sleep than usual?

Yes… yeah, I think so. It’s not every single night, but there have been nights where I stay up really late working, like I’ll be deep in a piece or revising something, and then I’ll only sleep maybe two or three hours. And normally that would ruin me the next day—I’d be dragging, irritable, needing coffee just to function—but lately I’ll wake up feeling kind of bright, like my eyes open and I’m immediately ready to keep going.

It feels strange because it doesn’t feel like “I didn’t sleep.” It feels more like I took a quick nap and then my brain is just… back on. Like there’s this sense of momentum, and I’ll think, okay, I can keep working, I can answer messages, I can get back into the studio. I know logically two or three hours isn’t much, but in the moment I don’t feel tired the way I usually would.
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people don’t?

Yeah… I mean, I’m hesitant to say it that way because it sounds so dramatic, but yes, there have been a few times when I’m alone in the studio and I hear what sounds like a woman’s voice. Not loud, not like someone shouting—more like she’s behind the shelves or over by the storage area, quietly commenting on what I’m doing. It’ll be just enough that I turn around because it feels like someone is actually there.

And the weird part is that in the moment it doesn’t feel like imagination. It feels completely real, like I’m about to find someone standing there, and then I check and there’s nobody. The studio is empty.

There’s also been this smell sometimes, like hot metal, almost scorched or heated metal, near an unfinished piece. I’ll look around thinking maybe something electrical is wrong or a tool got left on, but there’s nothing there. No one else seems to notice it, and when I try to find where it’s coming from, it just sort of… isn’t there.
Have there been times when you heard that voice even when your mood and energy felt completely normal?

Yes… that’s actually one of the things that worries me, because it wasn’t only when I was barely sleeping or feeling really sped up.

There was this quieter stretch—maybe about a month—where I was sleeping more normally, not perfect, but more like a regular amount for me. I didn’t have that unstoppable feeling, like I had to keep working and could do everything at once. I remember thinking, okay, maybe things are settling down.

But even then, in the studio, I would still hear those comments from behind the shelves. It would be quiet, almost like someone talking under their breath about what I was doing, and I’d stop and listen because it felt separate from me. And I’d still catch myself looking at ordinary materials—labels, scraps, packaging, notes, even the way things were stacked—and feeling like there were hidden warnings in them. Like they were telling me something I needed to notice.

That went on for several weeks, even though my mood and energy felt pretty normal compared to the more intense times. So… yes, I think it has happened outside of those energized periods.
During these more intense times, have you felt unusually euphoric or unusually irritable?

Yes. During those times I feel… almost lit from the inside, I guess. Like everything I’m thinking is important, and every idea connects to another idea, and I’ll feel really sure that I’m finally doing the work I’m supposed to be doing. It’s not just “in a good mood,” it’s more like this huge sense of, I can do anything, I can finish everything, I can make something brilliant if people would just keep up.

But it can flip really fast. Like if a collaborator makes some small comment—something normal, like questioning a material choice or saying a piece needs more time—I can snap. And I know afterward that my reaction was too big for what they said, but in the moment it feels like they’re blocking the whole thing or insulting the entire vision. I get sharp, defensive, sometimes angry in a way that feels disproportionate.

So yes, both, I think. There’s the euphoric, unstoppable part, but also this irritability where tiny things feel unbearable.
For at least one month altogether, have you been hearing the woman’s voice or feeling that ordinary things contain hidden warnings?

Yes… definitely more than a month. I wish it were just a short stretch, but when I try to lay it out honestly, it’s been happening on and off for maybe… around eleven months now.

Not every single day, and not always at the same intensity, which is part of why I kept trying to explain it away. But the voice in the studio, the feeling that materials or notes or labels had warnings in them, and sometimes those strange smells near the work—it’s all been part of the same long period. It would quiet down sometimes, and I’d think maybe it was gone, but then it would happen again.

So yes, altogether it’s well over a month. Roughly eleven months, I think.
Was there ever a period of at least two weeks when you were hearing the woman’s voice or noticing hidden warnings, while your mood felt completely normal?

Yes. I think that quieter month is the clearest example of that.

I wasn’t feeling high or unstoppable then. I was sleeping more normally—maybe not perfect, but much closer to normal for me—and I wasn’t in that mode where I felt like I had endless energy or like everything I was making was suddenly urgent and brilliant. My mood felt… pretty level, honestly. Not amazing, not terrible, just kind of normal.

But during that same stretch, I was still hearing the woman’s voice in the studio. It was usually like comments from behind the shelves, quiet enough that I’d freeze and listen, because it didn’t feel like it was coming from my own thoughts. And I was still looking at ordinary studio things—labels, scraps, packaging, materials sitting around—and feeling like there were warnings hidden in them, like I was supposed to decode something.

That went on for several weeks, so yes, at least two weeks. It wasn’t only happening when my mood was intense.
